questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to make your home smell nicer
Why some people can't smell anything
Why smell is so important to the feeling of being at home
How perfume is made
questions.why: They find out why our sense of smell is so important to feeling at home.

questions.q: What makes Phil feel at home?
options: Sleeping in his own comfortable bed at night
Relaxing on the sofa in his living room
The view from his window
Playing with his pet
questions.why: Phil says it's 'just relaxing on my sofa, in my living room'.

questions.q: Which smells remind presenter Tristan Ahtone of home?
options: His mother's perfume and his father's soap
Pine trees, damp and his grandad's old books
Fresh bread and coffee
Burning toast and smoke
questions.why: Tristan says, 'I know my mom's perfume, my dad's preferred soap.'

questions.q: According to Tristan, why might your house smell strange after a long trip?
options: Because the neighbours have been cooking
Because your nose gets tired and confused after travelling a long way
Because the air outside is cleaner
Because you notice its normal smell, which you usually ignore
questions.why: He says you might be smelling your home as it usually smells, but you just don't notice it there.

questions.q: Why can't we usually smell our own home?
options: Our homes have no smell
We clean them too often
Our noses stop working properly when we are indoors
The brain ignores it because it isn't a danger
questions.why: The brain analyses smells for danger, and your home's smell isn't a threat to you.

questions.q: Why does Tristan mention burning toast?
options: To show the brain quickly notices unusual smells that may mean danger
To explain why kitchens smell bad
To give advice about making breakfast
To show that we can't smell any food that is cooking in our own kitchen
questions.why: Filtering out common smells makes it easier to detect unusual ones, like toast starting to burn.

questions.q: Why does the smell of home still matter, even if we don't notice it?
options: It helps us sleep longer
It keeps insects away
It is connected with our feelings of comfort and safety
It helps us remember directions and find our way home again
questions.why: Tristan says it's 'entangled with our recognition of comfort and security'.

questions.q: According to Phil, which part of the brain is affected by the smell of home?
options: The part of the brain that controls how our body moves
The limbic system, which handles memory and emotion
The part that controls hearing
The part that helps us speak
questions.why: Phil says the scent affects the limbic system, which handles memory and emotion.
